title.narrative: Improvement of temporary housing conditions for vulnerable populations displaced by the earthquakes in southern Türkiye

description.narrative:
The massive earthquakes that struck southern Türkiye in the early hours of the 6th February, 2023 have caused widespread devastation, affecting over 20 million people, and causing over 50,000 deaths. The earthquakes also had a severe impact on the built environment in Türkiye, impacting over 4 million buildings. The Ministry of Environment, Housing and Climate Change’s rapid damage assessment concluded that at least 650,000 housing units in 229,000 buildings are either demolished, heavily damaged or moderately damaged and needing to be demolished and reconstructed. The Turkish Government has announced its intention to prioritise the demolition and reconstruction of heavily damaged buildings, leaving a number of gaps in the recovery process for other actors to fill. This destruction initially caused an estimated 2.7 million people to be displaced from their homes, with many of them remaining in tent settlements or other temporary accommodation. The Turkish Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency (AFAD) has distributed approximately 700,000 tents and established 209 container cities composed of 108,000 containers.
In order to assess the situation and identify suitable interventions, UN-Habitat deployed a surge mission to the affected area between the 26th February and the 6th March. The agency’s Executive Director Ms. Maimunah Mohd Sharif and Chief of Staff Dr. Erfan Ali also visited the region at the end of February, holding talks with local and national officials. Since before the earthquake, UN-Habitat has ongoing Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with the affected municipalities of Gaziantep an Osmaniye, providing a framework for collaboration on a diverse range of issues and establishing a physical presence for the agency in Gaziantep. Through discussions with the municipalities, the surge mission team identified a number of priority areas where UN-Habitat support would be imperative.
This project aims to support residents, especially vulnerable residents such as the elderly, the injured and people living with disabilities, by improving the thermal comfort of their container shelters throughout the hot summers and cold winters experienced in the region.
